mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer demand measured by HOUST coincides with stronger S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate future earnings growth.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the correlation between HOUST and 5-day SPX forward returns falls below 0.3, or 5-day returns are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A surge in employment as indicated by PAYEMS leads to increased consumer confidence and equity valuation expansion, driving positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: In regimes with high unemployment, the same PAYEMS movement produces negative or no forward returns (p-value > 0.05 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation rate crosses above 2%, the S&P 500 60-day forward return turns negative as market anticipates rate hikes.
failure_condition: No significant negative 60-day forward returns when CPIAUCSL crosses above 2% in non-inflationary regimes (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests weakening demand, which typically precedes a decline in equity valuations and negative 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: During contractionary phases, INDPRO declines are not associated with negative 20-day SPX returns (correlation < -0.2, p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both HOUST (consumer) and RSAFS (retail) indicates robust demand across sectors, producing positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: In periods of sector-specific weakness, the interaction of HOUST and RSAFS does not predict 5-day forward returns (IC < 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in UNRATE below 4% suggests labor market softening, which historically precedes a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as investors rotate into value stocks.
failure_condition: UNRATE remains below 4% but 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.5 percentage points in a month, the S&P 20-day forward return turns negative as discounting of future cash flows increases.
failure_condition: No significant negative 20-day returns when FEDFUNDS increases by >0.5pp in non-tightening regimes (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in INDPRO for three consecutive months signals structural supply-side weakness, which is associated with positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns as investors price in recovery.
failure_condition: INDPRO declines are not followed by positive 60-day forward returns in more than 40% of cases (binomial test p > 0.6).
